title: Merge conflict
whyItExists: Two people can change the same line at the same time. Git cannot guess which one is right, so it stops and asks. A conflict is a question, not an error.
recap: When two people edit the same lines, Git marks the clash in the file and waits for a person to decide. You keep the right parts of both changes, remove the markers, and commit. Pulling before you push finds the clash on your own computer, before anyone else is affected.

ticket.description: The constant does not say which currency it is in. Rename it so the unit is clear.

steps.prompt: Priya, the project manager, has assigned you a ticket. Read her message and choose a reply.

chat.message: ORD-24 is on the board and assigned to you. The constant DELIVERY_FEE does not say which currency it is in. Rename it to DELIVERY_FEE_USD.

replies.response: Thanks. Pull the latest main first, so you start from the newest code.

replies.text: Can I push it straight to main?
replies.response: No. Work on your own branch and open a pull request, so tests and a review happen before it goes live. Pull the latest main first.

steps.prompt: Pull the latest main before you start. Type the command below.
steps.hint: The command is git pull origin main. It brings in everything your teammates added since you last pulled.

steps.prompt: Move ORD-24 from To do to In progress, so the team can see you have picked it up.
steps.hint: Drag the ORD-24 card to the In progress column.

steps.prompt: Create your own branch for this ticket. Put the ticket number in the name, for example feature/ORD-24-delivery-fee-usd.
steps.hint: The command is git checkout -b followed by the branch name. A good name starts with feature/ or fix/ and includes ORD-24.

steps.prompt: In src/config.js, rename DELIVERY_FEE to DELIVERY_FEE_USD. Leave the value as it is.

steps.prompt: Save your change as a commit, with a message that says what changed.
steps.hint: Run git add . and then git commit -m followed by a message in quotes, for example "ORD-24 Rename DELIVERY_FEE to DELIVERY_FEE_USD".

changes.src/config.js:
export const TAX_RATE = 0.08
export const DELIVERY_FEE = 3.0
export const MAX_ITEMS = 40

steps.prompt: Tomás pushed a change to main. Read the message and choose a reply.

chat.message: I just pushed the new delivery fee to main, for ORD-25. It is 3.0 now. It is already in.

replies.text: Thanks. I'll pull main before I push and sort out any overlap.
replies.response: Good. If we touched the same line, Git will tell you when you pull, and you can fix it on your own computer.

replies.text: Mine is ready too. I'll push it and the last one in wins.
replies.response: Git does not work like that. It will not quietly pick a winner, it will stop on a conflict and someone has to decide by hand. Pull main first and look at both changes.

steps.prompt: Pull main into your branch before you push. Because you both changed the same line, Git will stop on a merge conflict. That is expected.
steps.hint: The command is git pull origin main. Git will say CONFLICT and mark the file.

steps.prompt: Git has stopped on a merge conflict in config.js. The file now has <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>> lines around the delivery fee. Keep both changes: your name DELIVERY_FEE_USD and Tomás's value 3.0. Delete the marker lines.
steps.autoFill:
export const TAX_RATE = 0.08
export const DELIVERY_FEE_USD = 3.0
export const MAX_ITEMS = 40
steps.hint: Between <<<<<<< and ======= is your version, and below ======= is Tomás's. Write one line with your name and his value, then delete the three marker lines.

steps.prompt: Finish the merge: stage the file and commit it.
steps.hint: Run git add . and then git commit -m followed by a message in quotes, for example "Merge main into my branch".
steps.autoFill:
git add .
git commit -m "Merge main into ORD-24-delivery-fee-usd"

steps.prompt: Pull once more before you push. It should say Already up to date.
steps.hint: The command is git pull origin main.

steps.prompt: Push your branch to GitHub so the team can see it.
steps.hint: The command is git push -u origin followed by your branch name.

steps.prompt: Raise a pull request asking your teammates to review your branch.
steps.hint: Give it a title that matches the ticket.

steps.prompt: Automated tests run on your pull request. Watch the result.
A teammate reads the change and approves it.
Tests passed and the change is approved. Merge the pull request into main.
The merged change is released to the live app.

replay.you: You started work without pulling the latest main.
replay.result: On a real team your branch would miss Tomás's change (the new delivery fee on the same line). Your pull request would show as out of date, and the gap grows with every hour you wait.

replay.you: You created your branch from an out-of-date copy of main.
replay.result: Your work starts from old code. Reviewers see a branch that does not match main, and merging it gets harder the longer it stays that way.

replay.you: You named your branch something that does not point to the ticket.
replay.result: Teammates cannot tell what the branch is for, and nobody can find it from ORD-24.

replay.you: You committed your change directly on main.
replay.result: Your change would skip review. Anyone who pulls main would get half-finished work.

replay.you: You wrote a commit message that does not say what changed.
replay.result: Months later nobody can tell why that line changed without opening the code, and searching the history finds nothing.
If a teammate had pushed to the same branch in the meantime, Git would have rejected your push and you would have had to untangle it afterwards.
The live app would be built from code that nobody reviewed and no test ran on, so a typo could break the app for every customer.

replay.you: You raised a pull request from an out-of-date branch.
replay.result: GitHub would show "This branch is out-of-date with the base branch", and your reviewer would wait for you to update it before they could trust the result.

replay.you: You said you would push your version and let the last change win.
replay.result: Git does not let the last change win quietly. It stops on a conflict. If someone forces it through, a teammate's work disappears and nobody notices until a customer does.

replay.you: You committed the file while the <<<<<<< and >>>>>>> lines were still in it.
replay.result: The markers are not code. The file would no longer build, the tests would fail, and everyone who pulled it would get a broken file.
